C-ATTEMPT-LOG.Summary: Record every attempt rather than only outcomes, bound churn at two, and escalate to replan rather than abort — on a fold that no longer destroys the evidence.
C-ATTEMPT-LOG.Problem:
The ledger cannot hold an attempt. buildEpochNode (grace-cursor.ts:735-769) folds each loose event into the ledger as exactly id, task and kind, with no children; the fold's verify step (:343-353) compares writtenEvents.length against events.length — a count, not a comparison — and the delete step (:367-375) unlinks every loose file on that verdict. Reproduced through the real CLI at 235f0f8: an event carrying outcome="fail", ordinal="1" and a FailureSignature child folds to <Event id="2" task="T-001" kind="attempt" />, run/ is emptied, and the command prints "Fold applied ... Events: 3". A confident success report about data it destroyed (A18.2, correction 31). Every field this change exists to record would be lost before the first review.
The grammar is not the defect and must not be blamed for it: validateRunLedgerArtifact (artifact/grammar.ts:628-732) never enumerates Event attributes and accepts a richer event happily. Reading either file alone hides the loss.
Unknown event kinds silently mean "still working". The kind-to-state map is a closed ternary with a fall-through default at two independent sites — advanceCursor (:235-236) on the write path and derivePosition (:465) on the read path, with the branches in opposite order. kind is unvalidated free-form input (advance --kind). An escalation event therefore reports in-progress, and fixing only the writer leaves the reader re-deriving in-progress the moment the cursor is regenerated (A18.5, correction 34).
A written cursor's state is an unchecked cast: state: (stateText as CursorState) || "idle" (:438). Any string in run.xml becomes a CursorState. That is nearly harmless while state is advisory and becomes load-bearing the moment a gate refuses to move past paused-pending-approval (A19.2).
Nothing can answer "did a write land between two attempts". listRepositoryChangedFiles (:620-652) is repository-wide, answers only for the moment it is called, and returns available: false when git cannot be reached — the branch that forced stateAbsence into existence in Phase 3 (A18.6, correction 35).

Goals.Goal: Attempts are ordinary run events carrying D2's allocated id. No ordinal is persisted — it is derived by counting a task's attempts in id order (A18.3).
The attempt outcome is three-valued, reusing Phase 2's AbsenceValue. A verification that could not run produces a verification-unavailable event, never an attempt (A18.4, A19.1).
A dumb counter (D9): the budget counts attempt events and inspects nothing. The exemption for an unran verification lives on the recording side, so no condition enters the counter (A19.1).
Budget exhaustion transitions to paused-pending-approval, a new CursorState value, surfacing both failure signatures and never claiming the task failed (A19.2).
One shared exhaustive kind-to-state map replacing both ternaries, with an explicit unknown-kind branch. An unrecognized kind must not mean "still working" (A18.5).

The written cursor's state is parsed against the union, not cast. An unrecognized value takes the existing degradation path rather than throwing — the mechanism recovers, lint reports (A19.2, invariant 3, anti-pattern 9).
Flake classification is a read over the ledger using write evidence snapshotted onto each attempt event, never a live git call at report time (A19.3, D8).
The execute skill states the budget and the escalation rule, mirrored byte-identically into the packaged tree.

Constraints.Constraint: The fold fix lands before any attempt type exists. Writing evidence into a shredder is not a sequencing preference (A19.3).
No ordinal, no timestamp and no second identity on any persisted event. Ordering is by allocated id (D2, §0.2, anti-pattern 6).
The counter contains no condition. "Dumb except here" is how clever counters begin (D9).
No second absence vocabulary. Reuse AbsenceValue and skills/ngrace/ngrace-cli/references/verdicts.md (D13, anti-pattern 5 and 10).
2 is a named constant carrying D9's "judgment, not derived" note beside it (§4.7 gate 3).
Attempt recording follows the cursor advance precedent — it writes what the executor just produced. It is not gated behind --apply (A18.7, invariant 8).
No event is overwritten. Every attempt appends (D6, §4.7 gate 2).
Additive only. A .ngrace tree with no attempt events lints clean — no issue, no migration (invariant 5).
Every authored path resolves through resolveContainedProjectPath (artifact/paths.ts:92).
skills/ngrace/* is source of truth; plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/* stays byte-identical in the same commit (invariant 1, §12.2).
No new runtime dependencies. No Phase 5+ constructs: no gate declarations, no transition surface, no reviewer automation, no confidence field.
AffectedAreas derives from the traced code path, never from §4.3's provisional file table (A5.6).

NonGoals.NonGoal: Gate declarations and the transition surface (Phase 5), including the gate that will refuse `applied` without a plan (A17.2) and the "no open epoch" archive precondition (A10.10 §1).
Reviewer automation and mechanized audits (Phase 6), including A15.4's report schema.
Deterministic failure localization (Phase 7) — this change records signatures, it does not localize with them.
Confidence recording and the calibration report (Phase 9).
Validating loose run/ event files through lint. The fold owns event validation (A11.2).
Making an escalated, unfoldable epoch foldable. The interaction is recorded in A18.5 §1 and belongs to Phase 5's precondition work.
The file-to-module ObservedWriteScope cross-check (A5.7; still unowned).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FOLD-PRESERVES-PAYLOAD:
Correction 31 (A18.2), and the phase's first task. buildEpochNode carries event attributes and children into the ledger rather than the three-attribute literal at grace-cursor.ts:735-769, and the fold's verify step compares written payload against the loose events rather than comparing lengths at :343-353.
The discriminating negative, which is the criterion and not an extra: a fold whose serializer drops a field must FAIL its own verify and leave every loose file on disk. Prove it by injection, the way AC-FOLD-ORDERING proved the write-verify-delete order in C-RUN-LEDGER — a test that only asserts payload survives a correct fold would have passed at 235f0f8, before this change existed.
Both directions per A7.2, since verify is a detection boundary: what newly fails (an event whose payload was dropped) and what still passes (an unchanged three-attribute event; a re-fold with nothing loose, :282-297; the concurrent-append case from C-RUN-LEDGER).
Report the probe from A18.2 re-run against the fix: the same loose event, the resulting ledger, and the state of run/. Verbatim.
While on this line, :344 reads events.filter((e) => e.kind !== "opened" || true) — a constant predicate making the filter a no-op inside an if that repeats the comparison. Remove it.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-EVENTS:
Correction 32 (A18.3). Attempts are run events with D2's allocated id, task and kind. A task that passes first time produces one attempt event; a task that fails then passes produces two, both present in the ledger AFTER fold — asserted against the folded ledger, not against loose files, because loose-file assertions are what correction 31 made vacuous.
No ordinal is persisted. grep the diff: no ordinal, sequence or index field on any event type. Ordinal shown in output is derived by counting a task's attempts in id order, and one test proves the derived ordinal survives a fold unchanged.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-THREE-VALUED-OUTCOME:
Correction 33 (A18.4) and A19.1. The attempt outcome is pass, fail, or absent — the third modelled on the shipped complete/completeAbsence pair (grace-cursor.ts:78-79, returned together at :574). No new absence vocabulary: AbsenceVerdict and AbsenceValue (:44-49) are reused as-is.
A verification that could not run produces a verification-unavailable event carrying the absence value and its reason — an event, never a silence. One test proves it appears in the folded ledger; that test fails if correction 31 regresses.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DUMB-COUNTER:
D9 and A19.1. Two tests, and the first is §4.5.2's discriminating negative kept verbatim from the plan: two failures with DIFFERENT signatures still exhaust the budget. Without it a later optimization makes the counter clever and nothing notices.
Its sibling: two verification-unavailable events in a row do NOT exhaust the budget, and both appear in the folded ledger. A test asserting only the count would pass while the events vanished.
The counter body contains no condition on signature, kind or content — it counts attempt events. The exemption is on the recording side (A19.1). 2 is a named constant with D9's "judgment, not derived" note beside it (§4.7 gate 3).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ESCALATION:
A19.2. CursorState gains paused-pending-approval (grace-cursor.ts:35). On the second failed attempt: record the exhaustion event, transition to paused-pending-approval, and surface both failure signatures. The output names both signatures and does not claim the task failed — shown verbatim.
The A5.4 drop-site inventory for CursorState in the phase report, each site file:line marked widened, deliberately unchanged with reason, or not on the path. The inventory in A19.2 is the starting point measured at 235f0f8, not the answer: re-measure. writeCursorFile's round-trip (:835-841) is verified by test rather than by reading, since it special-cases one existing value already.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-KIND-STATE-MAP:
Correction 34 (A18.5). One shared exhaustive kind-to-state map replaces BOTH ternaries — advanceCursor :235-236 and derivePosition :465 — with an explicit unknown-kind branch. An unrecognized kind must not resolve to in-progress.
Two sites is the criterion, not one: a test proves that after recording an escalation, DROPPING the cursor and re-deriving from the ledger still reports paused-pending-approval. A writer-only fix passes every other test here and fails this one.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CURSOR-STATE-PARSED: A19.2. The cast at :438, state: (stateText as CursorState) || "idle", is replaced by a parse against the widened union. A run.xml carrying an unrecognized state value takes the existing degradation path (CursorPosition.degradation, :88, set at :422 and :445, reported at :675) and cursor show still answers — it does not throw and does not block (invariant 3, anti-pattern 9). lint still reports the written file. One test asserts exactly that pairing, matching AC-RECOVER-NOT-BLOCK's shape in C-RUN-LEDGER.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FLAKE-CLASSIFICATION:
Correction 35 (A18.6) and A19.3. Each attempt event carries the write evidence observed when it was recorded. Classification compares two recorded snapshots and issues no git call at report time — a live call would classify the same ledger differently on different days, which is non-determinism in a record whose purpose is durability (D1).
Three fixtures, three verdicts: fail then pass with no intervening write is flaky; fail then pass with a write between them is a normal retry; and — the case the step as written omits — fail then pass where the write evidence was unavailable (listRepositoryChangedFiles returning available: false, :620-652) is unable-to-determine, neither flaky nor retry. Asserting flaky on unchecked evidence is anti-pattern 1.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ADDITIVE: Invariant 5 demonstrated, not asserted: polyglotFixture(), minimalTsFixture(), scaleFixture(20), examples/ and bun run ngrace lint --path . each yield zero new codes (§0.7.4). A ledger written before this change folds and reads identically after it. A new error on a previously-green project is release-breaking; do not edit a fixture to suit a check.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SKILL-TEXT: The budget and escalation rule reach the executor: skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md states when an attempt is recorded, what exhaustion does, and that escalation is a pause awaiting a decision rather than a failure. One or two sentences; never restate codes the binary emits (D13, anti-pattern 10). plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md byte-identical in the same commit. bun run validate:marketplace passes; line and token delta reported (§0.5, D15).

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The A18.2 probe re-run against the fix — loose event, resulting ledger, state of run/ — verbatim. The injected payload-drop fold showing verify failing and the loose files surviving. The A7.2 both-directions table for the fold's verify boundary. The drop-the-cursor, re-derive-from-ledger test output proving both kind-to-state sites were fixed. The A5.4 drop-site inventory for CursorState, re-measured. The escalation output naming both failure signatures. The three flake fixtures with their three verdicts. The §0.7.4 sweep across all five targets. The mutation-check table with no zero rows, or the discriminating negative added for each. The adversarial probe covering the five track-specific categories in §0.7.3.

Assumptions.Assumption: §4.2's precondition re-measured at 235f0f8 (A18.1): Phase 3 is COMPLETE, src/grace-cursor.ts is present at 1136 lines, and C-RUN-LEDGER is archived with spec and plan both applied.

A18's corrections 31-36 and A19's three answers govern where they disagree with §4.4 and §4.5. §4.4's AttemptEvent pseudocode is superseded: it predates Phases 2 and 3, has no event id, and its two-valued outcome is correction 28 repeated.

Every line citation here was measured at 235f0f8 and verified against the file rather than transcribed (A5.5). Re-measure before depending on one. A18.5's second kind-to-state site at :465 was found only because a citation was checked — expect the same of this document.

The write-surface baseline includes src/grace-cursor.ts as of Phase 3 (AC-WRITE-SURFACE in C-RUN-LEDGER). This change adds no new write surface and no new destructive operation; the greps must show exactly that.

An escalated task's epoch cannot fold, because validateEventsAgainstAllocations (:727-730) requires a terminal event in every allocation. That is recorded (A18.5 §1) and out of scope here; this change must not work around it by emitting a terminal event on escalation.
Path-only modules without LINKS remain warning-level and deliberate; the existing graph.module-without-linked-files warnings are the expected clean state.
